Primitive Custom Gradient

Source: R/primitives.R
prim_custom_gradient.Rd

Calls fn on args, but differentiates the result with rule instead of through the operations fn performs. Use it where those operations give no gradient – e.g. a prim_while() loop, which gradient() cannot differentiate – or an inaccurate one, while the derivative has a formula of its own.

Usage

prim_custom_gradient(args, fn, rule)

Arguments

args

(named list())
The arguments of fn: arrayish values, or trees of them in the sense of pjrt's RTree, by name. rule gives the gradient with respect to these. No entry may be named out, grad or required, the names under which rule receives the result, its gradient and which gradients are required. An R value materializes at its default data type, as in prim_while().

fn

(function)
Computes the result from the entries of args, which it receives as arguments. Returns an array, or a tree of them.

rule

(function | anvl_rule_reverse)
Computes the gradient. A function receives the entries of args as arguments, plus out, the result of fn, grad, the gradient with respect to out, of the same structure, data types and shapes, and required, a named logical() with one element per entry of args: TRUE where the gradient with respect to that entry is required, i.e. where any of its arrays requires one. Returns a named list with the gradient with respect to each required entry – for an array x, the sum over the elements of out of their grad times their derivative with respect to x – of x's structure, data types and shapes. An entry that is not required, e.g. an integer, which never is, can be left out or be NULL.

Alternatively, a rule_reverse() with a forward pass, which replaces fn where the result is differentiated, so that the backward pass can read what the forward pass computed. Its passes are those of a primitive's rule, except that inputs are the entries of args by name rather than one array per operand, params is an empty list, and outputs, grads, required and the returned gradients are those of a function above.

Value

(arrayish | list)
The result of fn.

Gradients

rule is traced when the gradient is, once the function being differentiated has been traced. It can close over constants – R values and arrays – but not over a traced value: pass that through args instead.

fn may close over traced values, but gradient() cannot differentiate with respect to those, as rule only gives the gradient with respect to args. Pass such a value through args instead.

Implemented Rules

  • stablehlo

  • quickr

  • reverse

StableHLO

Lowers the operations of fn in place. rule is not lowered: a gradient is traced, as anvl operations, before the program is lowered.

See also

gradient()

Examples

# x^n by repeated multiplication: a while loop, which gradient() cannot
# differentiate on its own
pow_loop <- function(x, n) {
  prim_while(
    init = list(i = 1L, y = x),
    cond = function(i, y) i < n,
    body = function(i, y) list(i = i + 1L, y = y * x)
  )$y
}
pow <- function(x, n) {
  prim_custom_gradient(
    list(x = x, n = n),
    fn = pow_loop,
    rule = function(x, n, out, grad, required) list(x = grad * n * x^(n - 1L))
  )
}
x <- nv_scalar(2)
pow(x, 3L)
#> AnvlArray
#>  8
#> [ CPUf32{} ] 
# the derivative 3 * x^2
jit(gradient(pow, wrt = "x"))(x, 3L)
#> $x
#> AnvlArray
#>  12
#> [ CPUf32{} ] 
#> 
# and, as it is computed from x, the second derivative 6 * x
dpow <- function(x, n) gradient(pow, wrt = "x")(x, n)$x
jit(gradient(dpow, wrt = "x"))(x, 3L)
#> $x
#> AnvlArray
#>  12
#> [ CPUf32{} ] 
#> 

# With a forward pass, x^(n - 1) is computed once, for the result and for
# its gradient
pow_fwd <- function(x, n) {
  prim_custom_gradient(
    list(x = x, n = n),
    fn = pow_loop,
    rule = rule_reverse(forward = function(inputs, params, required) {
      p <- inputs$x^(inputs$n - 1L)
      list(
        outputs = p * inputs$x,
        backward = function(inputs, outputs, grads, params, required) {
          list(x = grads * inputs$n * p)
        }
      )
    })
  )
}
jit(gradient(pow_fwd, wrt = "x"))(x, 3L)
#> $x
#> AnvlArray
#>  12
#> [ CPUf32{} ] 
#>
